messages:
nina: Heads-up: customer Sparrow submitted LoRA merge (adapter_v3) and our quick smoke shows weird rounding on invoice amounts. can we triage?
sanjay: sending the merge diff and baseline eval pack. diff: applied to models/sparrow/adapter_v3, scale=0.35. eval pack: https://redwood.dev/evals/sparrow-billing-quick2026
rachael: quick checks: tokenizer ids match, but notice token-splitting around currency symbols changed slightly. could be token boundary + quantization combo.
dave: i've kicked off two runs: (1) fp16 baseline + fp16 LoRA, (2) int4 base + fp16 LoRA. using smoke_billing.json golden set. command: ```./scripts/run_smoke --model sparrow:adapter_v3 --quant PROFILE --prompts smoke_billing.json --out /tmp/out.json```
sanjay: run1 (fp16/fp16) results: numeric exact-match 99.3%, formatting OK. run2 (int4 base) results: 97.4%, most diffs are cents rounding and dropped ‘$’.
rachael: try explicit kvcache warmup and prefix-cache disabled. sometimes cached KV offsets + low-precision kernels shift tokenization alignments.
dave: re-run with 10 warm queries + kv_prefix_cache=false. int4 case improved to 98.9% — still below threshold. latency p95 improved slightly with warmup.
ninja: (typo, ignore)
sanjay: hypothesis: quantized base kernels are altering softmax temperature at token boundaries leading to symbol-drop. LoRA in fp16 mitigates but int4 base still risky for billing.
rachael: suggested mitigations: (a) recommend fp16 base for billing-critical routes, (b) enable kv_warmup on serving side, (c) add model-catalog flag auto_fallback_to_fp16_on_numeric_failure.
dave: i'll add a smoketest matrix: run golden billing suite across quant profiles and fail PRs if numeric exact-match < 98.5%.
smoke-bot: Job 90181 started on dedicated-pool-07. logs: https://redwood.dev/jobs/90181/logs
sanjay: also adding a short note for support: "sparrow-adapter_v3: avoid int4 base for money formats; if int4 required enable kv_warmup=10 and prefix_cache off"
nina: thanks — we should ship merge but with recommended config and catalog warnings. tagging @rachael for PR entry and @dave for smoketest. :thumbsup:
